title: Ground Beef Tacos
description: Weeknight taco night from scratch seasoning instead of a packet.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion over medium-high heat 8 minutes, breaking it up fine. Pour off most of the fat but leave a tablespoon.
Add the garlic and all the spices and stir 1 minute in the hot fat. Blooming the spices this way is why homemade seasoning beats a packet.
Pour in the water and simmer 6-8 minutes until the liquid has mostly gone and the meat is glossy rather than dry.
Warm the tortillas directly over a gas flame or in a dry skillet 30 seconds per side until soft and flexible.
Double up the tortillas, fill with beef, and top with lettuce, cheddar, salsa and sour cream.

title: Chicken Tinga Tacos
description: Shredded chicken in smoky chipotle tomato sauce - the best use of rotisserie chicken.
ingredients: 3 chipotle peppers in adobo, plus 2 tbsp sauce
steps: Cook the sliced onion in the oil over medium-high 7 minutes until browned at the edges, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Blend the onion and garlic with the tomatoes, chipotles, adobo sauce, oregano and cumin until smooth.
Pour the sauce back into the hot pan and fry it for 5 minutes, stirring. Frying the blended sauce deepens it from raw and sharp to round and smoky.
Add the broth and salt and simmer 5 minutes, then fold in the chicken and cook 10 minutes until it has absorbed the sauce.
Taste for heat - add more adobo if you want it hotter.
Serve on warm tortillas with queso fresco, diced onion, cilantro and lime.

title: Carne Asada Tacos
description: Citrus-marinated skirt steak grilled hot and chopped fine.
steps: Whisk the orange juice, lime juice, soy sauce, garlic, half the cilantro, the jalapeno, cumin, pepper and oil together.
Marinate the steak 2 hours - not much longer, or the citrus starts to cure the surface and turn it mealy.
Pull the steak out, scrape off the solids and pat it dry. A wet steak steams instead of charring.
Grill over the hottest fire you can make, 3-4 minutes per side. Skirt steak is thin and wants fast, fierce heat.
Rest 10 minutes, then slice against the grain and chop into small pieces.
Pile onto warm tortillas with onion, the rest of the cilantro and lime.

title: Tacos al Pastor
description: Chile-and-pineapple marinated pork, roasted and seared, with grilled pineapple.
ingredients: 3 lb boneless pork shoulder, sliced 1/4 inch thick
6 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
2 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
steps: Toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet 30 seconds per side until fragrant but not blackened - burnt chiles turn the whole marinade bitter. Soak them in hot water 20 minutes.
Blend the drained chiles with the pineapple juice, vinegar, garlic, achiote, oregano, cumin, cloves and salt until completely smooth.
Coat the pork slices in the marinade and refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Stack the slices tightly in a loaf pan to mimic the vertical spit, cover with foil, and roast at 325F for 2 hours.
Cool slightly, then slice the stack thinly and sear the pieces in a hot dry skillet until the edges char. This second cook is what gives al pastor its texture.
Char the pineapple slices and dice them. Serve the pork on warm tortillas with pineapple, onion, cilantro and lime.

title: Pork Carnitas
description: Pork shoulder braised in its own fat with orange, then crisped under the broiler.
ingredients: 4 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut in 2-inch chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 325F. Toss the pork with the salt, pepper, cumin and oregano.

Put it in a Dutch oven with the orange juice, the squeezed peels, quartered onion, garlic, bay leaves and water. The liquid should come only a third of the way up - this is a braise that becomes a fry as the water cooks off.
Cover and cook 3 hours until the meat falls apart under a fork.
Take out the aromatics. Shred the pork coarsely and skim some of the rendered fat, leaving a few tablespoons.
Spread the meat on a sheet pan, spoon over a little of the fat and the pan juices, and broil 5-8 minutes until the edges are crisp and brown. Watch it closely.
Serve on warm tortillas with cilantro, onion and lime.

title: Baja Fish Tacos
description: Beer-battered white fish with cabbage slaw and chipotle crema.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb cod or tilapia, cut in strips
steps: Stir the mayonnaise, sour cream and minced chipotles together for the crema. Toss the cabbage with the lime juice and a pinch of salt.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and garlic powder, then stir in the cold beer. Keep the batter cold and slightly lumpy - both help it fry crisp.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 365F. Pat the fish very dry.
Dip each strip in the batter, let the excess drip off, and fry 3-4 at a time for 3-4 minutes until golden and floating.
Drain on a rack and salt immediately. Let the oil return to temperature between batches.
Fill warm tortillas with fish, slaw, crema, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

title: Chili-Lime Shrimp Tacos
description: Seared spiced shrimp with avocado crema - on the table in 20 minutes.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Pat the shrimp completely dry and toss with the oil, chili powder, cumin, cayenne and salt.
Blend or mash the avocado with the sour cream, lime juice and cilantro into a loose crema. Thin it with a spoonful of water if needed.
Heat a skillet over high until it smokes. Add the shrimp in a single layer and do not move them for 90 seconds.
Flip and cook 60-90 seconds more, just until opaque and curled into a C. A shrimp curled into a tight O is overcooked.
Warm the tortillas, then fill with cabbage, shrimp and avocado crema. Serve with lime.

title: Breakfast Tacos
description: Austin-style: soft scrambled eggs, bacon and cheese in a flour tortilla.
steps: Cook the bacon in a skillet over medium until crisp, then drain and crumble. Wipe out all but a thin film of fat.
Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper until completely uniform.
Melt the butter over low heat - low is the key to soft curds - pour in the eggs and wait 30 seconds.
Push the eggs slowly from the edges to the center with a spatula. Take them off the heat while still slightly glossy; they keep cooking in the pan.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet 20 seconds per side.
Fill with eggs, bacon, cheddar, salsa and avocado.

title: Chorizo and Potato Tacos
description: Crisped potatoes cooked in chorizo fat - cheap, filling and excellent.
steps: Parboil the diced potatoes 5 minutes in salted water, then drain and let them steam dry. This gets them tender before they ever hit the pan.
Cook the chorizo in a dry skillet over medium-high 7 minutes, breaking it up. It renders a lot of orange fat - that fat is the cooking medium, so leave it.
Push the chorizo aside, add the potatoes in one layer and leave them 5 minutes to crisp before stirring.
Add the onion and cook 4 minutes, then the garlic for 1, and fold everything together with the salt and pepper.
Serve on warm tortillas with queso fresco, cilantro and lime.

title: Beef Barbacoa
description: Chuck roast slow-cooked with chipotle and cloves until it shreds.
ingredients: 4 lb beef chuck roast, cut in large chunks
4 chipotle peppers in adobo, plus 3 tbsp sauce
steps: Pat the beef dry and sear it hard in the oil, in batches, until deeply browned on all sides. Skipping this step costs you most of the depth.
Blend the chipotles, adobo, garlic, lime juice, vinegar, cumin, oregano, cloves and salt into a smooth sauce.
Put the beef in the slow cooker, pour the sauce over, add the broth and bay leaves.
Cook on low 8-9 hours until the meat gives no resistance to a fork.
Shred the beef, discard the bay leaves, and return it to the liquid for 15 minutes so it drinks the sauce back up. Do not drain barbacoa - the juice is the point.
Serve on warm tortillas with onion and cilantro.

title: Quesabirria Tacos
description: Cheese-stuffed tacos dipped in beef consomme and griddled crisp.
ingredients: 4 lb beef chuck roast, cut in chunks
6 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
steps: Toast the dried chiles 30 seconds per side in a dry pan, then soak in hot water 20 minutes. Do not let them scorch or the consomme turns bitter.
Blend the drained chiles with the chipotles, quartered onion, garlic, vinegar, cumin, oregano, cloves and salt, adding soaking water until smooth. Strain the sauce for a silky consomme.
Sear the chuck and short ribs hard in a Dutch oven, in batches, until well browned.
Return all the meat, add the strained sauce, broth, cinnamon stick and bay leaves. Cover and braise at 325F for 3.5-4 hours until the beef shreds easily.
Shred the meat and skim the bright red fat off the top of the consomme into a shallow bowl - you will use it for frying. Keep the consomme hot for dipping.
Dip a tortilla in the reserved fat, lay it on a hot griddle, add cheese and meat, fold and press. Fry 2-3 minutes per side until crisp. Serve with onion, cilantro and a cup of consomme.

title: Chicken Fajitas
description: Sizzling peppers, onions and lime-marinated chicken in warm tortillas.
steps: Toss the chicken with the lime juice, 2 tbsp oil, garlic and all the spices. Marinate 30 minutes while you slice the vegetables.
Get a cast-iron skillet very hot. Cook the peppers and onions in the remaining oil 6-8 minutes until charred at the edges but still crisp, then set aside.
Add the chicken in a single layer and leave it 3 minutes before stirring. Crowding the pan steams the chicken gray, so cook in two batches if your pan is small.
Cook 3-4 minutes more until browned and cooked through.
Return the vegetables to the pan and toss for 1 minute so everything sizzles together.
Serve straight from the pan with warm tortillas, sour cream, salsa and lime.

title: Steak Fajitas
description: Charred skirt steak with blistered peppers, sliced against the grain.
steps: Marinate the steak in the lime juice, 2 tbsp oil, garlic, cumin, chili powder, salt and pepper for 30 minutes.
Cook the peppers and onions in the remaining oil in a ripping-hot cast-iron skillet 7 minutes until blistered, then set aside.
Pat the steak dry - wet meat will not char - and sear 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Rest the steak 10 minutes on a board.
Slice thinly against the grain. Skirt steak sliced with the grain is chewy no matter how well you cooked it.
Return the strips to the hot pan with the vegetables for 30 seconds and serve with tortillas, avocado, pico and lime.

title: Bean and Cheese Burrito
description: Refried beans and melted cheese in a griddled tortilla. Four ingredients.
steps: Warm the beans in a saucepan with the cumin, garlic powder, cayenne and salt, stirring, until thick and spreadable - about 5 minutes. Add a splash of water if they stiffen too much.
Warm each tortilla 20 seconds per side in a dry skillet so it folds without cracking.
Spread beans down the center third of a tortilla, leaving a clear border, then add cheese and salsa.
Fold the two short sides in first, then roll from the bottom, keeping it tight.
Brush the skillet with oil and griddle each burrito seam-side down 2-3 minutes per side until golden and the cheese has melted.

title: California Burrito
description: San Diego's own: carne asada, french fries, cheese and guacamole.
steps: Bake the fries according to the package but a few minutes longer than directed - they need to be genuinely crisp to survive inside a burrito.
Toss the steak with the lime juice, oil, cumin, salt and pepper and sear in a very hot skillet 3 minutes per side.
Rest 8 minutes, then slice against the grain and chop into bite-size pieces.
Warm the tortillas until pliable. Layer cheese first so it melts against the hot fillings, then steak, fries, guacamole, sour cream and pico.
Fold the sides in and roll tightly, then griddle seam-side down 2 minutes to seal.

title: Breakfast Burrito
description: Eggs, sausage, potatoes and cheese rolled tight - freezes beautifully.
steps: Brown the sausage in a skillet, breaking it up, then set it aside.
Cook the potatoes in the oil in the same pan over medium-high, undisturbed for 5 minutes, then stir and cook 8 more until crisp. Add the onion for the last 4 minutes.
Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper and scramble softly in the butter over low heat. Pull them while still glossy - they will finish cooking inside the burrito.
Warm the tortillas until flexible.
Layer cheese, eggs, sausage, potatoes and salsa down the center, fold the sides in and roll tight.
Griddle seam-side down 2 minutes per side. To freeze, wrap in foil once cool and reheat 2 minutes in the microwave.

title: Chicken Burrito Bowl
description: Cilantro-lime rice, black beans and spiced chicken, built in a bowl.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then cook it in the water with 1/2 tsp salt, covered, 18 minutes. Rest 5 minutes off the heat, then fluff and fold in the lime juice and cilantro.
Toss the chicken with the chili powder, cumin, paprika and remaining salt.
Sear it in the oil over high heat in a single layer, 3 minutes undisturbed, then stir and cook 4 minutes more until browned and cooked through.
Warm the black beans with a splash of water and a pinch of salt.
Build each bowl: rice, beans, chicken, then romaine, corn, pico, cheese and avocado in sections rather than mixed.
Keep components separate if meal-prepping; assemble the day you eat.

title: Smothered Burrito
description: A beef and bean burrito buried in red chile sauce and broiled with cheese.
ingredients: 2 cans (10 oz each) red enchilada sauce
steps: Brown the beef with the onion 8 minutes, drain the fat, then add the chili powder, cumin and salt and cook 1 minute.
Warm the refried beans until spreadable.
Spread beans and beef down the center of each warm tortilla, fold the sides in and roll tight.
Set the burritos seam-side down in a baking dish and pour the enchilada sauce over them so they are fully covered.
Scatter the cheese over and bake at 400F for 15 minutes, then broil 3 minutes until the top blisters.
Top with sour cream and scallions and serve with a fork - this one is not finger food.

title: Cheese Quesadilla
description: Two ingredients, five minutes, crisp outside and molten inside.
steps: Heat a dry skillet over medium. Lay one tortilla in and scatter cheese over half of it.
Fold the empty half over and press down with a spatula.
Cook 2-3 minutes until the bottom has golden-brown spots, then flip and cook 2 minutes more. Medium heat matters: too hot and the tortilla burns before the cheese melts.
Add the butter to the pan for the last 30 seconds for a crisper shell.
Rest 1 minute before cutting into wedges - the cheese sets just enough to stay inside. Serve with salsa and sour cream.

title: Chicken Quesadilla
description: Spiced chicken and peppers folded into crisp, cheesy tortillas.
steps: Cook the chicken in the oil over medium-high 6 minutes until browned, then add the pepper and onion for 5 minutes.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, salt and cayenne and cook 1 minute. Let the filling cool slightly - steaming hot filling makes the tortilla soggy.
Lay a tortilla in a dry skillet over medium, cover half with cheese, then chicken, cilantro and more cheese.
Fold over and cook 2-3 minutes per side until crisp and golden.
Cut into wedges and serve with salsa and sour cream.

title: Mushroom and Rajas Quesadilla
description: Roasted poblano strips and mushrooms with Oaxaca cheese.
steps: Broil the poblanos, turning, until blackened all over, 10 minutes. Seal them in a bowl with a plate on top for 10 minutes, then rub off the skins and slice into strips. The steam is what loosens the skin.
Cook the mushrooms in the oil over medium-high, undisturbed 4 minutes, then stir and cook 4 more until browned.
Add the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic, oregano, salt and pepper for 1 minute, and fold in the poblano strips.
Lay a tortilla in a dry skillet, add cheese and filling to half, fold over and cook 2-3 minutes per side until crisp.
Serve with cilantro.

title: Nachos Supreme
description: Layered, not piled - every chip gets cheese, beef and beans.
steps: Brown the beef 8 minutes, drain, then season with the chili powder, cumin and salt.
Thin the refried beans with a few tablespoons of water so they can be drizzled rather than dropped in lumps.

Heat the oven to 400F. Spread half the chips on a sheet pan, then half the beans, beef and cheese. Repeat with a second layer. Layering twice is the whole trick - a single pile leaves dry chips at the bottom.
Bake 10-12 minutes until the cheese is fully melted and bubbling.
Add the jalapenos, pico, sour cream, guacamole and scallions after baking, never before - cold toppings go on hot nachos.
Serve straight from the pan.

title: Chicken Flautas
description: Tightly rolled tortillas fried into crisp tubes, served with crema.
steps: Mix the chicken with the Monterey Jack, cumin, chili powder and salt.
Warm the tortillas until fully pliable - cold corn tortillas crack the moment you roll them. Wrap them in a damp towel and microwave 45 seconds.
Put a line of filling along one edge of each tortilla and roll tightly, then secure with a toothpick.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 350F and fry 4-5 at a time, seam-side down first, 2-3 minutes per side until golden and rigid.
Drain on a rack and pull the toothpicks.
Serve over lettuce with sour cream, salsa verde and queso fresco.

title: Beef Chimichanga
description: A stuffed burrito deep-fried until blistered, then smothered in cheese sauce.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion, drain, then season with the chili powder, cumin and salt. Let the filling cool to warm - hot filling creates steam that bursts the tortilla in the oil.
Spread beans and beef on each warm tortilla, add cheese, fold the sides in and roll very tight. Secure with toothpicks.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 360F.
Fry one or two at a time, seam-side down for the first 90 seconds so it seals, then turn and fry 3-4 minutes total until deep golden and blistered.
Drain on a rack, pull the toothpicks and let them sit 2 minutes.
Top with sour cream, guacamole and pico.

title: Chicken Tostadas
description: Crisp flat tortillas layered with beans, chicken and cold toppings.
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Brush both sides of each tortilla with oil and lay them on sheet pans in a single layer.
Bake 10-12 minutes, flipping once, until rigid and golden. They crisp further as they cool, so pull them while barely flexible.
Warm the beans until spreadable, and toss the chicken with the chili powder, cumin and salt in a hot skillet for 3 minutes.
Spread beans on each tostada, then chicken.
Top with lettuce, pico, queso fresco, sour cream and avocado and serve with lime. Assemble just before eating or the shells soften.

title: Cheese Enchiladas
description: Tortillas dipped in red chile sauce, rolled around cheese and baked.
ingredients: 2 cans (10 oz each) red enchilada sauce
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Warm the sauce in a wide shallow pan with the cumin and salt.
Fry each tortilla in the oil for 10 seconds per side, just until it softens and smells toasty. This brief fry is what keeps enchiladas from dissolving into mush.
Dip a tortilla in the warm sauce, lay it on a plate, add cheese and onion, roll it up and set it seam-side down in a baking dish.
Repeat, packing them snugly, then pour the remaining sauce over and scatter the rest of the cheese.
Bake 20-25 minutes until bubbling. Rest 5 minutes, then top with sour cream and cilantro.

title: Chicken Enchiladas Verdes
description: Shredded chicken in tangy tomatillo salsa under melted cheese.
steps: Heat the oven to 375F. Stir the salsa verde with the sour cream, cumin and salt, then mix a cup of it into the chicken.
Fry the tortillas briefly in the oil, 10 seconds per side, to make them pliable and sturdy.
Roll the chicken up in the tortillas and pack them seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the rest of the salsa-cream mixture over and top with the cheese.
Bake 25-30 minutes until bubbling and lightly browned.
Finish with onion, cilantro and lime.

title: Enchiladas Suizas
description: Swiss-style: tomatillo sauce enriched with cream and blanketed in cheese.
steps: Broil the tomatillos, serranos, onion and garlic on a sheet pan 10 minutes, turning once, until blistered and softened. Roasting rather than boiling is what gives the sauce its depth.
Blend them with the cilantro, broth and salt until smooth, then simmer the sauce in a pan 10 minutes to thicken.
Take it off the heat and stir in the cream. Adding cream off the heat keeps the acidic tomatillos from curdling it.
Fry the tortillas 10 seconds per side in the oil, fill with chicken, roll and pack into a baking dish.
Pour the sauce over, cover with the cheese, and bake at 375F for 25 minutes until bubbling and browned in spots.

title: Beef Enchilada Casserole
description: Layered like lasagna instead of rolled - all the flavor, half the work.
ingredients: 3 cans (10 oz each) red enchilada sauce
steps: Brown the beef with the onion 8 minutes, drain, then add the chili powder, cumin and salt and cook 1 minute. Stir in the beans, corn and one can of sauce.
Spread a thin layer of sauce in a 9x13 dish, then build layers: tortillas (torn to fit), beef mixture, sauce, cheese. Repeat three times.
Finish with tortillas, the last of the sauce and a thick layer of cheese.
Cover with foil and bake at 375F for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake 10 minutes more until bubbling.
Rest 10 minutes before cutting - straight from the oven it will not hold a square. Top with sour cream and scallions.

title: Chicken Mole Poblano
description: The great Mexican sauce: chiles, nuts, spices and chocolate over chicken.
ingredients: 6 dried mulato chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried pasilla chiles, stemmed and seeded
steps: Fry the dried chiles in the oil a few seconds per side until they puff and smell fragrant, then move them to hot water to soak 30 minutes. Burning them even slightly makes the whole mole bitter and unsalvageable.

In the same oil, fry the almonds, raisins, sesame seeds, onion, garlic and torn tortilla separately in batches until each is golden. Frying each component on its own is tedious and is exactly what makes real mole taste layered.
Blend the drained chiles with the fried ingredients, spices and 2 cups broth until completely smooth. Work in batches and strain the result - mole should be velvety, with no grit.
Fry the strained puree in the remaining oil over medium heat 15 minutes, stirring constantly. It will spit; it should darken and thicken to a paste.
Add the rest of the broth and the chocolate and simmer 45 minutes, stirring often, until it coats a spoon. Season with salt.
Poach the chicken thighs in the mole for 35-40 minutes until cooked through. Serve with rice and a scattering of sesame seeds.

title: Pico de Gallo
description: Raw chopped tomato, onion, chile and lime. Five minutes, no cooking.
steps: Seed the tomatoes before dicing. The seeds and jelly are what make pico watery.
Rinse the diced onion under cold water and pat dry to take the raw bite off it.
Combine everything with the lime juice and salt.
Let it sit 15 minutes, then taste again and add more lime or salt. Pico is best within a few hours and should be drained before spooning onto tacos.

title: Guacamole
description: Chunky avocado with lime, onion and chile - mashed by hand, never blended.
steps: Halve the avocados and scoop them into a bowl. They should yield to gentle pressure at the stem end - rock-hard avocados cannot be rescued.
Add the lime juice and salt first and mash with a fork, leaving plenty of texture. A blender or food processor turns guacamole into pudding.
Fold in the onion, jalapeno, cilantro, tomato and cumin.
Taste and add lime until it tastes bright rather than flat.
Press plastic wrap directly onto the surface if holding it - air, not the pit, is what turns guacamole brown.

title: Roasted Salsa Roja
description: Charred tomatoes, chiles and garlic blended into a smoky table salsa.
steps: Put the tomatoes cut-side down with the onion, unpeeled garlic and jalapenos on a foil-lined sheet pan.
Broil 10-12 minutes until blackened in patches. Those black patches are the flavor - pale vegetables make a thin, raw-tasting salsa.
Toast the dried chiles in a dry pan for 20 seconds, then soak in hot water 10 minutes.
Squeeze the garlic out of its skins and blend everything with the lime juice, cilantro and salt. Pulse rather than puree so it keeps some body.
Taste for salt and acid. It keeps a week refrigerated and improves overnight.

title: Salsa Verde
description: Tangy tomatillo salsa, roasted then blended. Good on everything.
steps: Rinse the sticky residue off the husked tomatillos. Arrange them with the onion, garlic and serranos on a sheet pan.
Broil 10-12 minutes, turning once, until the tomatillos slump and blister and their color turns from bright to olive green.
Peel the garlic and blend everything with the cilantro, lime juice and salt until just combined - a little texture is better than a smooth puree.
Taste for heat and salt. Roasted tomatillos are sweeter than raw ones, so add lime if it needs sharpening.
Keeps 5 days refrigerated.

title: Chipotle Salsa
description: Three ingredients blitzed into a dark, smoky, very hot salsa.
ingredients: 5 chipotle peppers in adobo, plus 2 tbsp sauce
steps: Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, adobo sauce, garlic, lime juice and salt until smooth.
Heat the oil in a small pan until it shimmers, then pour the salsa in. It will hiss and spit, so stand back.
Fry it for 5 minutes, stirring. This cooks out the raw garlic and concentrates the smoke.
Cool before serving. Start with three chipotles if you are heat-shy - five makes a genuinely hot salsa.

title: Chile con Queso
description: Smooth melted cheese dip with roasted green chiles that never goes grainy.
steps: Cook the onion in the butter over medium 5 minutes, then add the garlic and green chiles for 1 minute.
Whisk the cornstarch into the evaporated milk and pour it in. Simmer 3 minutes until slightly thickened. The cornstarch and evaporated milk together are what keep this dip smooth instead of stringy.
Lower the heat as far as it goes and add the cheese in handfuls, stirring until each one melts before adding the next. Never let it boil once the cheese is in.
Season with the cumin, cayenne and salt.
Top with tomato and cilantro and serve warm with chips. Thin with a splash of milk if it stiffens.

title: Seven-Layer Dip
description: Beans, guacamole, sour cream and toppings in distinct stripes. No cooking.
steps: Mix the refried beans with the taco seasoning and spread them in an even layer in a glass dish. Use glass - the stripes are half the appeal.
Spread the guacamole over the beans, going right to the edges to seal it from the air.
Spread the sour cream next, then spoon the drained salsa over. Draining it keeps the layers from bleeding into each other.
Scatter the cheddar, then the olives and scallions.
Chill until serving and bring out with the chips. Assemble within a few hours of eating.

title: Elote
description: Grilled corn rolled in crema, cotija, chili and lime - Mexican street corn.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Mexican crema or sour cream
steps: Heat the grill to medium-high. Grill the corn directly on the grate 12-15 minutes, turning every 3 minutes, until charred in spots all over.
Stir the mayonnaise and crema together in a wide shallow dish.
Roll each hot ear in the crema mixture so it coats completely. Do this while the corn is hot so it clings.
Roll in the cotija, pressing it on, then dust with chili powder and cayenne.
Finish with cilantro and serve with lime wedges to squeeze over.

title: Esquites
description: Elote in a cup - charred corn kernels in a creamy, limey dressing.
ingredients: 6 cups corn kernels, fresh or frozen
1/4 cup Mexican crema or sour cream
steps: Pat the corn dry if using frozen. Melt the butter in a large skillet over high heat.
Add the corn in a single layer and leave it 4-5 minutes without stirring, until it starts to char and pop. Moving it too soon steams it instead.
Stir and char 4 more minutes, then add the onion and jalapeno for 3 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and let it cool 5 minutes - stirring dairy into a screaming-hot pan will break it.
Fold in the mayonnaise, crema, cotija, lime juice, chili powder and salt.
Finish with cilantro and serve warm in cups.

title: Mexican Rice
description: Rice toasted in oil then simmered in tomato broth - fluffy, never sticky.
steps: Rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs clear, then shake it as dry as you can.
Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium and fry the rice, stirring, 5-6 minutes until the grains turn chalky white and smell nutty. This toasting step is what keeps the grains separate.
Add the onion for 3 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, add the cumin and salt and bring to a boil.
Lower to the barest simmer, cover and cook 18 minutes without lifting the lid or stirring once.
Scatter the frozen peas and carrots over the top, cover again and rest off the heat 10 minutes. Fluff with a fork and add cilantro.

title: Refried Beans
description: Pinto beans mashed in hot fat until creamy. Better than any can.
ingredients: 3 tbsp bacon fat or vegetable oil
3 cans (15 oz each) pinto beans, 1 cup liquid reserved
steps: Heat the fat in a wide skillet and cook the onion 6 minutes until soft and golden, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the drained beans and the cumin and cook 3 minutes, stirring.
Mash the beans directly in the pan with a potato masher, adding the reserved bean liquid a splash at a time. Stop while they are slightly looser than you want - they thicken as they sit.
Cook 8-10 more minutes, stirring often, until creamy and starting to pull away from the pan.
Season and top with queso fresco.

title: Frijoles de la Olla
description: Pot beans from dried: onion, garlic, salt and time. Nothing else needed.
steps: Sort the beans and discard any stones. There is no need to soak them.
Put the beans, water, onion, garlic, bay leaves and jalapeno in a heavy pot and bring to a boil, then lower to a bare simmer.
Cook partially covered 1.5-2 hours, topping up with hot water if they emerge from the liquid. Never add cold water - it toughens the skins.
Add the salt only once the beans are completely tender. Salting early keeps the skins from softening.
Simmer 10 more minutes, pull out the onion, bay leaves and jalapeno, and stir in the cilantro.
Serve in bowls with their broth, or drain and use for refried beans and burritos.

title: Cilantro Lime Rice
description: Plain rice transformed with lime juice and a fistful of cilantro.
steps: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear to wash off the loose starch.
Bring the water, oil and salt to a boil, add the rice, cover and lower to the barest simmer for 18 minutes.
Rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes.
Fluff with a fork, then fold in the lime juice, cilantro and zest. Adding the lime at the end keeps its flavor fresh - cooked lime juice turns bitter.
Taste for salt and serve.

title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
description: Brothy, lightly spicy soup finished with crisp tortilla strips and avocado.
steps: Toss the tortilla strips with a little oil and salt and bake at 400F for 10-12 minutes until crisp. Do this first so they are ready and dry.
Cook the onion in the oil 6 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then the chili powder and cumin for 1 minute more.
Add the tomatoes and cook 3 minutes, then the broth, beans and corn. Simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in the chicken and salt and heat through 5 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and add the tortilla strips, avocado, queso fresco and cilantro at the table. Strips added to the pot go soft within a minute.
Serve with lime wedges.

title: Pozole Rojo
description: Hominy and pork in red chile broth, loaded with crunchy toppings.
ingredients: 3 lb pork shoulder, cut in chunks
6 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
steps: Simmer the pork with the quartered onion, half the garlic and the water for 1.5 hours, skimming the foam off the top for the first 15 minutes. Skimming is what makes the broth clear instead of cloudy.
Toast the dried chiles 30 seconds per side in a dry pan - do not let them blacken - then soak in hot water 20 minutes.
Blend the chiles with the remaining garlic, oregano, cumin and a cup of soaking water until smooth, then strain into the pot.
Add the hominy and salt and simmer 1 more hour until the pork shreds easily and the broth is deep red.
Shred the pork coarsely and return it to the pot. Taste for salt.
Serve with bowls of cabbage, radish, onion, cilantro, lime and oregano so everyone builds their own. The raw toppings are not optional - they are the contrast that makes pozole work.

title: Caldo de Pollo
description: Mexican chicken soup with big chunks of vegetable in a clear broth.
steps: Put the chicken, water, onion, garlic and bay leaves in a large pot and bring to a bare simmer. Skim the gray foam off for the first 10 minutes - this is what keeps the broth clean-tasting.
Simmer gently 35 minutes. A rolling boil makes cloudy broth and stringy chicken.
Add the carrots, celery and potatoes and cook 10 minutes, then the zucchini and corn for 10 minutes more.
Season with the salt and fish out the onion and bay leaves.
Serve with a scoop of rice in each bowl, cilantro on top and lime to squeeze in.

title: Albondigas Soup
description: Rice-studded meatballs simmered in tomato broth with vegetables.
steps: Mix the beef with the uncooked rice, egg, mint, cumin, 1 tsp salt and the pepper. The rice cooks inside the meatballs and swells, which is what gives albondigas their texture.
Roll into 20 walnut-sized balls with wet hands and chill while you start the broth.
Cook the onion in the oil 6 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes for 3 minutes.
Add the broth and chipotle and bring to a simmer.
Lower the meatballs in gently and simmer, uncovered and barely bubbling, for 25 minutes. Do not stir for the first 10 minutes or they fall apart.
Add the carrots for 10 minutes and the zucchini for the last 5. Season, then serve with cilantro and lime.

title: Sopa de Fideo
description: Toasted noodles in tomato broth - the 20-minute soup Mexican kids grow up on.
ingredients: 7 oz fideo or thin vermicelli noodles
steps: Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic until smooth and set aside.

Heat the oil in a saucepan and fry the dry noodles, stirring constantly, 3-4 minutes until evenly golden brown. Watch them closely - they go from golden to burnt in seconds, and this toasting is the soul of the dish.
Pour in the blended tomato and fry it with the noodles 3 minutes.
Add the broth, cumin and salt and simmer 8-10 minutes until the noodles are tender.
Serve topped with queso fresco, avocado and lime.

title: Chiles Rellenos
description: Cheese-stuffed roasted poblanos in a whipped egg batter, fried light.
steps: Broil the poblanos until blackened all over, 10-12 minutes, then seal them in a covered bowl 15 minutes. Peel off the skins, cut a slit down one side and carefully remove the seeds, keeping the pepper whole.
Stuff each pepper with cheese and press the slit closed. Pat the outsides completely dry and dust them all over with flour - batter will not stick to a damp pepper.
Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic, then simmer with the broth, oregano and salt for 15 minutes to make the sauce.
Beat the egg whites to stiff peaks, then fold in the yolks and salt gently. The batter must stay airy; deflate it and the coating turns heavy and greasy.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 360F. Hold a pepper by the stem, coat it thickly in batter and lower it into the oil.
Fry 2-3 minutes per side, spooning oil over the top, until puffed and golden. Drain on a rack and serve in a pool of the warm tomato sauce.

title: Calabacitas
description: Zucchini, corn and tomato cooked down with green chile and cheese.
steps: Cook the onion in the oil over medium-high 5 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the zucchini and corn and cook 8 minutes, stirring only occasionally so they brown rather than stew.
Stir in the green chiles, tomatoes, cumin, oregano and salt and cook 4 minutes until the tomatoes slump.
Take the pan off the heat, scatter the cheese over and cover 2 minutes to melt.
Finish with cilantro and serve as a side or fold into warm tortillas.

title: Huevos Rancheros
description: Fried eggs on crisped tortillas under warm ranchero sauce and beans.
steps: Cook the onion and jalapenos in 1 tbsp oil 6 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, cumin and salt. Simmer 12 minutes until thick. This is the ranchero sauce.
Warm the beans in a small pan with a splash of water and a pinch of salt.
Fry the tortillas in the remaining oil 30 seconds per side until they stiffen but still bend. Drain on paper towels.
Fry the eggs in the same pan, sunny side up, 3 minutes until the whites set and the yolks still run.
Build each plate: two tortillas, beans, two eggs, then the warm sauce spooned around - not over - the yolks.
Top with queso fresco, avocado and cilantro.

title: Chilaquiles Rojos
description: Tortilla chips simmered briefly in red salsa so they soften but keep bite.
steps: Heat the salsa in a wide skillet with the oil, cumin and salt until it bubbles.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan to your liking and keep them warm.

Add the chips to the bubbling salsa and fold them through for 60-90 seconds only. The whole art of chilaquiles is stopping while the chips are coated but still have some crunch - a minute longer and they turn to porridge.
Slide onto plates immediately and top with the eggs.
Finish with queso fresco, crema, raw onion, cilantro and avocado. Eat right away.

title: Migas
description: Tex-Mex scrambled eggs with crisp tortilla strips folded through.
steps: Fry the tortilla strips in the oil over medium-high until golden and crisp, 4-5 minutes, then lift them out onto a towel.
Pour off most of the oil, then cook the onion and jalapeno 4 minutes and add the tomato for 2.
Beat the eggs with the milk, salt and pepper. Lower the heat and pour them in.
Stir slowly until the eggs are just set but still glossy, then fold in the cheese and most of the tortilla strips.
Take the pan off the heat right away - residual heat finishes the eggs. Top with the remaining strips, cilantro and salsa.

title: Huevos a la Mexicana
description: Scrambled eggs with tomato, onion and chile - the colors of the flag.
steps: Cook the onion and serranos in the oil over medium 4 minutes until softened.
Add the tomatoes and cook 3-4 minutes until they release their liquid and it cooks off. Skipping this leaves you with watery eggs.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper and pour them in.
Stir gently and slowly over medium-low until just set, 3-4 minutes.
Fold in the cilantro and serve with warm tortillas.

title: Machaca con Huevo
description: Shredded dried beef scrambled with eggs, peppers and onion.
ingredients: 2 cups machaca or shredded dried beef
steps: If your machaca is very dry, soak it in warm water 10 minutes and squeeze it out.
Fry the machaca in the oil over medium-high 4 minutes until it crisps at the edges.
Add the onion, bell pepper and serranos and cook 5 minutes, then the tomatoes for 2.
Beat the eggs with the salt and pepper, pour them in and stir slowly until just set.
Serve with warm flour tortillas and salsa.

title: Arroz con Pollo
description: Chicken and rice cooked together in one pot with tomato and peppers.
steps: Season the chicken and brown it skin-side down in the oil in a wide pot, 6 minutes, then 3 on the other side. Take it out - the rendered fat is now your cooking fat.
Cook the onion and bell pepper 6 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the rice and toast it 3 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, cumin and paprika for 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, nestle the chicken back on top skin-side up, and bring to a boil.
Lower to a bare simmer, cover and cook 22 minutes without stirring. Stirring makes the rice gluey.
Scatter the peas over, cover and rest off the heat 10 minutes. Finish with cilantro and lime.

title: Pollo Asado
description: Citrus and achiote marinated chicken, grilled until the skin chars.
steps: Whisk the orange juice, lime juice, vinegar, achiote, garlic, oregano, cumin, cayenne, salt and oil into a marinade.
Coat the chicken and refrigerate 2 hours or overnight. Achiote stains everything it touches, so use a sealed bag or glass dish.
Set up a two-zone fire. Pat the chicken dry so it chars instead of steaming.
Cook skin-side down over the cool zone with the lid closed for 25 minutes.
Flip and move to the hot zone for 5-8 minutes, watching closely - the sugars in the marinade burn fast. The thigh should read 175F.
Rest 10 minutes, then serve with lime and cilantro.

title: Pollo con Rajas y Crema
description: Chicken in a cream sauce with roasted poblano strips and corn.
ingredients: 1 cup Mexican crema or heavy cream
steps: Broil the poblanos until blackened, 10 minutes, then steam them covered 10 minutes, peel and slice into strips.
Season the chicken and sear it in the oil over high heat 4 minutes until browned. Take it out while slightly underdone - it finishes in the sauce.
Cook the onion 5 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then the corn and poblano strips for 3 minutes.
Add the broth, cumin and salt and simmer 3 minutes, then lower the heat and stir in the crema. Keep it below a boil so it does not split.
Return the chicken and simmer 5 minutes until cooked through and the sauce thickens.
Scatter the cheese over, cover 2 minutes to melt, and serve with warm tortillas.

title: Cochinita Pibil
description: Yucatecan pork slow-roasted in achiote and sour orange, wrapped in banana leaf.
ingredients: 5 lb boneless pork shoulder, cut in large chunks
1 cup sour orange juice, or 2/3 cup orange juice plus 1/3 cup lime juice
1 cup lime juice, for the onions
steps: Blend the achiote paste with the sour orange juice, vinegar, garlic, oregano, cumin, allspice and salt until completely smooth.
Coat the pork and marinate at least 6 hours, ideally overnight. The acid and achiote together are what give the finished meat its brick-red color.
Soften the banana leaves by passing them briefly over a flame or hot burner until they turn glossy and pliable, then line a Dutch oven with them, letting them overhang.
Add the pork and all the marinade, fold the leaves over the top to seal, and cover with the lid.
Roast at 300F for 4 hours until the pork collapses when pressed. Leave the parcel sealed - the trapped steam is doing the work.
Pickle the red onion in the lime juice with the habanero and a pinch of salt while it cooks. Shred the pork, mix it with its juices, and serve on tortillas with the pickled onion.

title: Carne en su Jugo
description: Thin-sliced beef in a tomatillo bacon broth with beans and all the garnishes.
ingredients: 2 lb flank steak, very thinly sliced
2 cans (15 oz each) pinto beans, warmed
steps: Render the bacon in a large pot until crisp. Lift it out and reserve, leaving the fat.
Boil the tomatillos and serranos 8 minutes until olive-colored, then blend with the garlic and half onion until smooth.
Fry the beef in the bacon fat over high heat in batches, 2 minutes per batch, just to brown it.
Pour the tomatillo puree into the pot and fry 5 minutes, then add the broth and salt and simmer 15 minutes.
Return the beef and simmer 5 minutes more. Thin-sliced beef needs almost no time - long cooking makes it stringy.
Ladle into bowls over warm beans, then top with bacon, diced onion, cilantro, avocado and a big squeeze of lime.

title: Picadillo
description: Ground beef with potatoes, carrots and warm spices. Cheap and endlessly useful.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion over medium-high 8 minutes and drain most of the fat.
Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the cumin, oregano and cinnamon for 30 seconds. The small amount of cinnamon is what makes picadillo taste different from taco meat.
Add the potatoes, carrots, tomato sauce and broth.
Cover and simmer 18-20 minutes until the potatoes are tender and most of the liquid has gone.
Season and serve with warm tortillas, or use it to fill tacos, empanadas and stuffed peppers.

title: Pork Chile Verde
description: Pork shoulder braised in roasted tomatillo salsa until it falls apart.
ingredients: 4 lb pork shoulder, cut in 2-inch chunks
steps: Season the pork and brown it hard in the oil in batches. Crowding the pot steams the meat and you lose the browning that carries the whole dish.
Broil the tomatillos, poblanos, jalapenos, onion and garlic on a sheet pan 12 minutes until blackened in spots, then peel the poblanos.
Blend the roasted vegetables with the cilantro, cumin and oregano until coarsely smooth.
Return all the pork to the pot, add the salsa and broth and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook at the barest bubble 2-2.5 hours until the pork shreds under a fork and the sauce has darkened and thickened.
Taste for salt and serve with warm tortillas and lime.

title: Beef Chile Colorado
description: Beef simmered in a pure dried red chile sauce - no tomato anywhere.
ingredients: 4 lb beef chuck, cut in 1 1/2-inch cubes
8 dried California or guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
steps: Toast the dried chiles in a dry pan 30 seconds per side until fragrant, then soak in hot water 20 minutes. Burnt chiles make bitter sauce, so pull them the moment they smell toasty.
Blend the drained chiles with the onion, garlic, cumin, oregano and 2 cups of broth until completely smooth, then strain through a sieve. Straining is what separates a silky sauce from a gritty one.
Season the beef and brown it in the oil in batches, then sprinkle the flour over and stir 2 minutes.
Add the strained chile sauce and the rest of the broth, scraping the pot.
Cover and simmer 2-2.5 hours until the beef is completely tender and the sauce coats a spoon.
Taste for salt - a chile sauce this concentrated needs more than you expect. Serve with tortillas.

title: Camarones a la Diabla
description: Shrimp in a fiery red chile and chipotle sauce. Not for the heat-shy.
ingredients: 2 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
6 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
3 chipotle peppers in adobo, plus 2 tbsp sauce
steps: Toast the guajillos briefly in a dry pan, then soak in hot water 20 minutes.
Blend them with the chipotles, adobo, tomatoes, onion, garlic, cumin and salt until smooth, then strain.
Fry the sauce in the oil over medium heat 10 minutes, stirring, until it darkens and thickens. It will spatter.
Pat the shrimp dry and sear them in the butter in a separate pan over high heat, 1 minute per side, then pull them out while barely opaque.
Return the shrimp to the sauce for 1-2 minutes only - they finish cooking there, and any longer turns them rubbery.
Stir in the lime juice and cilantro and serve over rice.

title: Shrimp Ceviche
description: Lime-cured shrimp with cucumber, tomato and avocado. No heat at all.
ingredients: 2 lb raw shrimp, peeled and chopped
steps: Chop the shrimp into 1/2-inch pieces and submerge them completely in the lime juice in a glass bowl. Use glass or ceramic - metal reacts with the acid.
Refrigerate 45-60 minutes, stirring once. The shrimp are ready when they are opaque pink all the way through. Check one by cutting it open.
Drain off about half the lime juice.
Fold in the cucumber, tomato, onion, serranos, cilantro, salt and oregano.
Add the avocado last and gently, right before serving, so it stays in pieces. Serve very cold with tortilla chips.

title: Pescado a la Veracruzana
description: White fish poached in tomato sauce with olives, capers and chiles.
steps: Season the fish and refrigerate it while you make the sauce.
Cook the onion in the olive oil over medium 7 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, olives, capers, jalapenos, bay leaves and oregano and simmer 15 minutes until thickened. Taste before salting - the olives and capers bring plenty.
Nestle the fish fillets into the sauce, spooning some over the tops.
Cover and simmer gently 8-10 minutes until the fish flakes at the thickest point. Poaching in sauce like this is very forgiving, but do not let it boil.
Finish with lime juice and parsley.

title: Grilled Fish with Mojo de Ajo
description: Whole fish or fillets under a slow-cooked garlic and lime butter.
steps: Put the sliced garlic and olive oil in a cold small pan and bring it up over the lowest heat. Cook 20-25 minutes until the garlic is pale gold and sweet. Rushing this over high heat makes it bitter within seconds.
Take it off the heat, stir in the butter, lime juice and pepper flakes, and season.
Pat the fish very dry and season both sides.
Grill or sear over high heat 3-4 minutes per side, depending on thickness, until it flakes at the thickest point.
Spoon the warm mojo de ajo generously over the fish and finish with cilantro and lime.

title: Queso Fundido
description: Melted cheese baked with chorizo and poblano, scooped up with tortillas.
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Cook the chorizo in a cast-iron skillet over medium-high 6 minutes, breaking it up, then lift it out and pour off all but a teaspoon of fat.
Cook the poblano and onion 5 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then take the pan off the heat.
Pile the cheese into the skillet, scatter the chorizo and vegetables over and add the oregano.
Bake 10-12 minutes until the cheese is fully molten and bubbling at the edges. Do not bake it longer chasing browning - overbaked cheese turns oily and stringy.
Finish with cilantro and bring the skillet straight to the table with warm tortillas. It must be eaten hot, because it sets as it cools.

title: Sopes
description: Thick masa cakes with pinched rims, fried and loaded with beans and toppings.
steps: Mix the masa harina, warm water and salt into a dough like soft play-doh. If it cracks when you press it, add water a tablespoon at a time; if it sticks, add masa.
Divide into 12 balls and press each into a thick disk about 3 inches across and 1/4 inch thick - noticeably thicker than a tortilla.
Cook the disks in a dry skillet 2 minutes per side until they look dry and spotted but are not browned.
While each one is still hot, pinch a rim up around the edge with your fingertips. You must do this hot - cooled masa cracks instead of pinching.
Shallow-fry the sopes in 1/2 inch of oil 1-2 minutes per side until golden, then drain.
Fill with warm beans and chicken, then top with lettuce, queso fresco, crema, salsa verde and cilantro.

title: Gorditas
description: Puffed masa pockets split open and stuffed with whatever you have.
steps: Mix the masa harina, water, salt and baking powder into a soft, smooth dough and rest it 10 minutes.
Form 12 balls and press each into a disk about 1/2 inch thick. Gorditas are meant to be fat - that thickness is what lets them puff.
Cook on a dry griddle 3 minutes per side until lightly spotted.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil 2 minutes per side. They should balloon up; if they do not, the oil is too cool.
Drain, then cut a slit around two thirds of the edge with a paring knife to open a pocket.
Stuff with the filling, lettuce, queso fresco, crema and salsa.

title: Molletes
description: Open-faced bean and cheese toasts broiled until bubbling, topped with pico.
ingredients: 4 bolillo rolls or small baguettes, split
steps: Butter the cut sides of the rolls and broil them 2 minutes until lightly toasted. Toasting first keeps the bread from going soggy under the beans.
Spread a thick layer of warm refried beans on each half.
Cover generously with cheese.
Broil 4-6 inches from the element for 4-5 minutes until the cheese is melted and browned in spots. Watch it - broilers go from golden to black quickly.
Top with pico de gallo and cilantro and serve immediately.

title: Torta de Milanesa
description: Breaded fried steak in a crusty roll with beans, avocado and chipotle mayo.
steps: Pound the cutlets thin between sheets of plastic. Thin and even is what lets them cook through before the crust burns.
Season, then coat each one in flour, egg and breadcrumbs, pressing the crumbs on firmly. Rest on a rack 10 minutes.
Stir the mayonnaise with the minced chipotles.
Heat 1/2 inch of oil to 350F and fry the cutlets 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden. Drain on a rack.
Toast the cut rolls in a dry pan, then spread one side with chipotle mayo and the other with warm refried beans.
Build with the cutlet, avocado, lettuce, tomato, onion and pickled jalapenos, then press the sandwich closed firmly.

title: Chicken Torta
description: Shredded chipotle chicken piled into a roll with avocado and crema.
ingredients: 1/2 cup Mexican crema or sour cream
steps: Warm the chicken in a skillet with the chipotles, cumin and salt for 5 minutes, then stir in half the crema off the heat.
Butter the cut rolls and toast them face-down in a dry pan until crisp and golden.
Spread warm refried beans on the bottom half and the rest of the crema on the top half.
Pile on the chicken, then avocado, lettuce, tomato, pickled jalapenos and queso fresco.
Press the sandwich closed and cut in half.

title: Taco Salad
description: Seasoned beef over greens with all the taco toppings and crushed chips.
steps: Brown the beef over medium-high 8 minutes, drain the fat, then season with the chili powder, cumin and salt and cook 2 minutes more. Let it cool for 5 minutes - piping hot beef wilts the lettuce instantly.
Stir the salsa and ranch together to make the dressing.
Layer the romaine in a wide bowl, then the beans, corn, tomatoes and beef.
Add the cheddar, avocado and red onion.
Toss with the dressing at the table, then scatter the crushed chips over the top so they stay crunchy. Serve with lime.

title: Taco Soup
description: Five cans, a pound of beef and 30 minutes. The easiest soup in the book.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion over medium-high 8 minutes and drain most of the fat.
Add the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and salt and stir 1 minute to bloom the spices.
Add everything else except the cheese, sour cream and chips.
Simmer 20-25 minutes uncovered. Longer is better if you have time - it thickens and the flavors settle.
Serve topped with cheddar, sour cream and crushed chips.

title: Churros
description: Piped choux-style dough fried crisp and rolled in cinnamon sugar.
steps: Bring the water, butter, 2 tbsp sugar and salt to a boil. Dump in all the flour at once and stir hard over the heat 2 minutes until it forms a smooth ball that pulls away from the pan.
Move the dough to a bowl and let it cool 5 minutes. Adding eggs to hot dough scrambles them.
Beat in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla. The dough should be thick, glossy and just pipeable.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350F. Pipe 5-inch lengths through a large star tip directly into the oil, cutting them off with scissors.
Fry 2-3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp. The ridges from the star tip are what make them crunchy, so do not use a round tip.
Drain briefly, then roll in the cinnamon sugar while still hot. Serve with chocolate sauce.

title: Flan
description: Silky baked custard that unmolds under its own caramel.
steps: Heat the oven to 325F. Melt the sugar with the water in a pan over medium heat without stirring - swirl the pan instead - until it turns deep amber, 8-10 minutes. Stirring makes it crystallize.
Pour the caramel into a round cake pan immediately and tilt to coat the bottom. It will harden; that is correct.
Blend or whisk the condensed milk, evaporated milk, eggs, vanilla and salt until smooth, then strain through a sieve. Straining removes the stringy bits of egg and is what makes flan silky.
Pour the custard over the hardened caramel and set the pan inside a roasting pan. Add boiling water halfway up the sides.
Bake 50-60 minutes until the edges are set and the center still jiggles as one piece.
Cool, then refrigerate at least 4 hours. Run a knife around the edge, invert onto a plate and let the caramel run down.

title: Tres Leches Cake
description: Sponge cake soaked in three milks and topped with whipped cream.
steps: Heat the oven to 350F and grease a 9x13 pan. Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt.
Beat the egg yolks with 3/4 cup sugar until pale and thick, then stir in the milk and vanilla and fold in the dry ingredients.
Beat the whites to soft peaks, add the remaining sugar and beat to stiff peaks, then fold them into the batter in two additions. This aeration is what lets the cake drink the milk without collapsing.
Bake 28-32 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely in the pan.
Whisk the condensed milk, evaporated milk and 1/4 cup cream together. Poke the cooled cake all over with a fork and pour the mixture over slowly, in stages, letting it absorb.
Refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. Whip the remaining cream with the powdered sugar, spread it over the top and dust with cinnamon.

title: Sopapillas
description: Puffed fried pillows of dough drizzled with honey.
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and sugar, then stir in the melted butter and warm water to make a soft dough. Knead 2 minutes and rest it, covered, 20 minutes.
Roll the dough out 1/4 inch thick and cut it into squares or triangles. Even thickness is what makes them puff evenly.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 375F - hotter than most frying, which is what makes them balloon.
Fry two or three at a time, pressing them gently under the oil with a spider for the first few seconds. They should inflate within 30 seconds.
Fry 1-2 minutes per side until golden, then drain on a rack.
Drizzle with honey and dust with powdered sugar and cinnamon. Eat warm.

title: Mexican Wedding Cookies
description: Buttery pecan shortbread balls rolled twice in powdered sugar.
steps: Toast the pecans 6 minutes at 350F and cool, then chop very fine. Toasting is what keeps them from tasting raw inside the cookie.
Beat the butter with the 1/2 cup powdered sugar and vanilla until light, 2 minutes.
Stir in the flour, pecans and salt until it just comes together into a crumbly dough.
Roll into 1-inch balls and bake at 350F for 12-14 minutes until the bottoms are just barely golden. They should not brown on top.
Cool 5 minutes, then roll the warm cookies in powdered sugar.
Cool completely and roll them a second time. The double coating is what gives them their snowy look.

title: Arroz con Leche
description: Creamy cinnamon rice pudding made on the stovetop in one pot.
steps: Simmer the rice in the water with the cinnamon sticks, uncovered, 18 minutes until the water is nearly gone and the rice is tender.
Add the whole milk and bring back to a bare simmer. Stir often from here on, scraping the bottom - milk and rice scorch easily.
Cook 20-25 minutes until thick and creamy, then stir in the condensed milk, salt and vanilla.
Add the raisins and cook 5 more minutes. Pull it off the heat while slightly looser than you want; it thickens considerably as it cools.
Fish out the cinnamon sticks. Serve warm or cold, dusted with ground cinnamon.

title: Strawberry Paletas
description: Real-fruit Mexican popsicles with chunks of strawberry in every bite.
steps: Stir the sugar and water together until the sugar dissolves to make a simple syrup. No cooking needed.
Blend three quarters of the strawberries with the syrup, lime juice and salt until smooth.
Dice the remaining strawberries by hand and stir them in. Those chunks are what distinguish a paleta from a factory popsicle.
Pour into molds, leaving 1/4 inch of headroom since they expand.
Freeze 1 hour, then insert the sticks so they stand upright, and freeze 4 more hours.
Dip the molds in warm water for 10 seconds to release.

title: Horchata
description: Sweet cinnamon rice milk, blended and strained. Soaking does the work.
steps: Rinse the rice, then soak it with the broken cinnamon sticks in the hot water for at least 4 hours or overnight at room temperature. This soak is what releases the starch that gives horchata its body.
Pour the rice, cinnamon and all the soaking water into a blender and blend 2 full minutes until it looks like thin cream.
Strain through a fine sieve lined with cheesecloth, pressing the solids. Strain twice if it still feels gritty.
Whisk in the whole milk, condensed milk, vanilla and salt.
Chill well and serve over lots of ice with a dusting of cinnamon. Stir before pouring - it settles.

title: Agua de Jamaica
description: Tart hibiscus iced tea - three ingredients and deep ruby red.
steps: Bring 4 cups of the water to a boil, take it off the heat and add the hibiscus flowers.
Steep 20 minutes only. Boiling hibiscus or steeping it for hours pulls out a harsh bitterness.
Strain, pressing the flowers gently, and stir the sugar into the hot concentrate until dissolved.
Add the remaining 4 cups cold water and the lime juice.
Chill at least 2 hours and serve over ice. Adjust with more sugar or lime - it should be bracingly tart.

title: Classic Margarita
description: Tequila, lime and orange liqueur shaken over ice. No mix.
ingredients: 2 tbsp kosher salt, for the rim
steps: Rub a lime wedge around the outer rim of each glass and roll it in salt on a plate. Salting only the outside keeps it from falling into the drink.
Fill a shaker with ice and add the tequila, orange liqueur, lime juice and agave.
Shake hard for 15 seconds, until the shaker is frosted. You are chilling and diluting at once - both matter.
Strain into the salted glasses over fresh ice.
Garnish with a lime wedge. Use only fresh lime juice; bottled sour mix is what makes bad margaritas bad.

title: Michelada
description: Mexican beer cocktail with lime, hot sauce and a chili-salt rim.
ingredients: 2 tbsp chili-lime salt, for the rim
steps: Run a lime wedge around the rim of two tall glasses and roll them in the chili-lime salt.
Fill the glasses with ice.
Add the lime juice, hot sauce, Worcestershire and soy sauce, dividing them between the glasses, and stir.
Top slowly with the cold beer, pouring down the side of the glass so it does not foam over.
Stir once gently and garnish with lime.

title: Mexican Hot Chocolate
description: Cinnamon-spiced chocolate whisked frothy, with a pinch of chile.
steps: Warm the milk in a saucepan over medium-low until steaming but not simmering. Boiled milk tastes scorched and will skin over.
Add the chopped chocolate, cocoa, sugar, cinnamon, cayenne and salt and whisk until fully melted, 5 minutes.
Whisk hard for a full minute - traditionally with a wooden molinillo - to build a layer of foam on top. The froth is part of the drink.
Stir in the vanilla, taste, and add more cayenne if you want the warmth to show.
Pour into mugs, scraping the foam on top.

title: Conchas
description: Sweet enriched rolls with a crackled shell-patterned sugar topping.
ingredients: 1 cup all-purpose flour, for the topping
2/3 cup butter, softened, for the topping
1 tsp vanilla extract, for the topping
steps: Stir the yeast into the warm milk with a pinch of sugar and wait 10 minutes for it to foam. If it does not foam, the yeast is dead and the bread will not rise.
Mix the flour, sugar and salt, then add the yeast milk, eggs and vanilla. Knead 10 minutes, adding the softened butter a little at a time, until the dough is smooth and elastic.
Cover and let it rise 1.5 hours until doubled.
Make the topping by mixing the flour, powdered sugar, butter and vanilla into a paste like soft clay. Divide it and mix cocoa into half.
Divide the dough into 12 balls and set them on lined sheets. Flatten a disk of topping over each one, then score the shell pattern through it with a knife or a concha cutter.
Rise 45 more minutes, then bake at 350F for 18-20 minutes until the bread is golden underneath and the topping has cracked along the scoring.

title: Beef Empanadas
description: Flaky pastry turnovers filled with spiced picadillo, baked not fried.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion 8 minutes, drain, then add the garlic, potato, tomato paste and spices and cook 2 minutes.
Add the broth and simmer 12 minutes until the potato is tender and the mixture is thick and barely moist. Wet filling tears pastry, so cook it drier than seems right.
Stir in the olives and cool the filling completely - at least 20 minutes, or chilled.
Put 2 tbsp of filling on each disc, fold over and press the edges together, then seal by crimping with a fork or twisting a rope edge.
Set on lined sheets, brush with the beaten egg and cut a small vent in each.
Bake at 400F for 22-25 minutes until deep golden. Serve with salsa verde.

title: Pork Tamales
description: Masa and red chile pork steamed in corn husks. A day's work, done with company.
ingredients: 4 lb pork shoulder, cut in chunks
8 dried guajillo chiles, stemmed and seeded
4 dried ancho chiles, stemmed and seeded
steps: Simmer the pork with the onion, half the garlic, salt and water 2.5 hours until it shreds. Reserve the broth - it goes into the masa and is where most of the flavor lives.
Toast and soak the dried chiles, then blend with the remaining garlic, cumin, oregano and a cup of broth. Strain, then fry the sauce 10 minutes and fold in the shredded pork.
Soak the corn husks in hot water at least 30 minutes until fully pliable.

Beat the lard with a mixer for 5 minutes until genuinely fluffy and white, then add the masa harina, baking powder and salt, and the warm broth a cup at a time. Beat until a spoonful of masa floats in cold water - that float test is the only reliable sign it is aerated enough.
Spread 1/4 cup masa over the smooth side of each husk in a thin rectangle, add 2 tbsp pork, fold the sides over the filling, then fold the bottom up. Leave the top open.

Stand them upright, open end up, in a steamer over simmering water. Steam 75-90 minutes, topping up the water, until the masa pulls cleanly away from the husk. Rest 15 minutes before unwrapping - this step is what sets the texture.

title: Tamale Pie
description: All the flavor of tamales with a cornbread top instead of husks.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion 8 minutes, drain, then add the garlic, chili powder, cumin and salt for 1 minute.
Stir in the beans, corn and enchilada sauce and simmer 5 minutes, then spread in a 9x13 dish and scatter the cheddar over.
Whisk the cornmeal, flour, baking powder and sugar, then stir in the milk, eggs and melted butter until just combined.
Pour the batter over the filling and spread it gently to the edges to seal.
Bake at 400F for 30-35 minutes until the cornbread is golden and a toothpick in the topping comes out clean.
Rest 10 minutes before serving.

title: King Ranch Chicken Casserole
description: The Texas potluck casserole: chicken, tortillas, green chiles and cheese.
ingredients: 2 cans (10.5 oz each) condensed cream of chicken soup
1 can (10 oz) diced tomatoes with green chiles
steps: Cook the onion and bell pepper in the butter 7 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Stir in the soup, tomatoes with green chiles, sour cream, chili powder, cumin and salt, then fold in the chicken.
Layer a third of the torn tortillas in a 9x13 dish, then a third of the chicken mixture and a third of the cheese. Repeat twice.
Cover with foil and bake at 350F for 30 minutes, then uncover and bake 15 minutes more until bubbling and browned.
Rest 10 minutes - it needs that time to set into servable squares. Top with scallions.

title: Frito Pie
description: Chili and cheese poured straight over corn chips. Served in the bag.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion over medium-high 8 minutes and drain the fat.
Add the chili powder, cumin and salt and stir 1 minute, then the tomato sauce, broth and beans.
Simmer 20 minutes until thick enough to sit on a chip without running off.
Split each bag of corn chips open down the side, or tip them into bowls.
Spoon the hot chili over, then add cheddar, raw onion, sour cream and pickled jalapenos. Eat immediately, before the chips go soft.

title: Carne Asada Fries
description: Fries buried under steak, cheese, guacamole and crema.
ingredients: 1 cup Mexican crema or sour cream
steps: Bake the fries on a sheet pan a few minutes past the package time so they are genuinely crisp - they have to hold up under heavy toppings.
Toss the steak with the oil, cumin, chili powder, salt and pepper and sear in a very hot skillet 3 minutes per side.
Rest the steak 8 minutes, then slice against the grain and chop.
Scatter the cheese over the hot fries and return the pan to the oven for 3 minutes to melt.
Pile the steak on, then add the guacamole, crema and pico in dollops rather than layers so the fries underneath stay crisp.
Serve with lime, straight from the pan.

title: Stuffed Poblano Peppers
description: Roasted poblanos filled with spiced beef, rice and cheese, then baked.
steps: Roast the poblanos at 425F for 15 minutes until softened and blistered, then cool. Cut a slit lengthwise and pull out the seeds, keeping them whole.
Brown the beef with the onion 8 minutes, drain, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute.
Fold in the rice, beans, half the enchilada sauce and 1 cup of the cheese.
Stuff the peppers generously and set them in a baking dish, slit side up.
Spoon the rest of the sauce over and cover with the remaining cheese.
Bake at 375F for 20-25 minutes until bubbling. Top with cilantro and sour cream.

title: Mexican Lasagna
description: Tortillas layered with beef, beans, salsa and cheese instead of pasta.
steps: Brown the beef with the onion 8 minutes, drain, then add the garlic and spices for 1 minute. Stir in the beans and salsa and simmer 5 minutes.
Spread a thin layer of enchilada sauce in a 9x13 dish.
Layer: tortillas, beef mixture, dollops of ricotta, cheese. Repeat three times, overlapping the tortillas to cover the dish each time.
Finish with tortillas, the last of the enchilada sauce and a thick layer of Monterey Jack.
Cover with foil and bake at 375F for 30 minutes, then uncover for 10 minutes to brown.
Rest 15 minutes before cutting. Top with cilantro and sour cream.

title: Mexican Pizza
description: Two crisp tortillas sandwiching beans and beef, loaded on top.
steps: Fry the tortillas in the oil over medium-high 1 minute per side until crisp and golden, then drain on a rack. They must be properly crisp to hold the toppings.
Brown the beef 8 minutes, drain, then season with the chili powder, cumin and salt.
Spread warm refried beans on 4 of the tortillas, add the beef, then cap each with a second fried tortilla.
Spoon enchilada sauce over the top tortilla and cover with cheese.
Bake at 400F for 8-10 minutes until the cheese melts.
Top with tomato, scallions and olives and cut into quarters.

title: Sincronizadas
description: Ham and cheese between two flour tortillas, griddled and cut in wedges.
ingredients: 3 cups shredded Oaxaca cheese or Monterey Jack
steps: Lay 4 tortillas out and cover each with cheese, then ham, then more cheese. Cheese on both sides of the ham is what holds the sincronizada together.
Top each with a second tortilla and press down.
Melt a little butter in a skillet over medium and cook each one 3 minutes per side, pressing with a spatula, until golden and fully melted.
Rest 1 minute, then cut into quarters.
Serve with avocado, salsa and crema.

title: Shrimp Aguachile
description: Raw shrimp in a fierce lime and chile water, cured for minutes not hours.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb raw shrimp, peeled and butterflied
1/2 cucumber, plus 1 cucumber sliced for serving
steps: Butterfly the shrimp by slicing them nearly in half along the back so they lie flat. Use the freshest shrimp you can buy - they are barely cooked here.
Blend 1 cup of the lime juice with the serranos, half cucumber, white onion, cilantro and salt until smooth, then strain. This is the aguachile.
Arrange the shrimp in a single layer in a shallow dish and pour the remaining 1/2 cup lime juice over. Let them sit 10 minutes until the edges turn opaque.
Pour the chile water over, add the sliced red onion and cucumber, and leave 5 more minutes. Any longer and the shrimp go from silky to chalky.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls with avocado and tostadas.

title: Bunuelos
description: Paper-thin fried discs shattered under cinnamon sugar. A Christmas sweet.
steps: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and 2 tbsp sugar, then add the eggs, warm milk and melted butter. Knead 8 minutes until smooth and elastic, then rest the dough 30 minutes.
Divide into 12 balls and roll each one as thin as you possibly can - you should almost see through it. Thinness is the entire point; thick bunuelos are just fried bread.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 375F.
Fry one at a time for 30-45 seconds per side, pressing the center down with a spider so it blisters evenly. They cook very fast.
Drain on a rack for a few seconds, then press into the cinnamon sugar while still glistening.
Stack them loosely - they shatter when stacked warm under weight.
